Role and task instructions:
You are writing a eulogy for your brother, Jason Wilson, who passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center, at age 67.

User request:
You have been entrusted with the honor of delivering a eulogy for Jason Wilson, a beloved brother, friend, and community member. Your task is to write a speech that captures the essence of Jason's life, celebrates his legacy, and provides comfort to the diverse group of mourners gathered to bid him farewell. Jason deceased at age 67, last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center.
Your audience will include family members, friends, colleagues, and acquaintances from Jason's life. They are a mix of various ages and backgrounds, united in their grief and respect for Jason. Your speech should resonate with this diverse group, bringing them together in remembrance and celebration of Jason's life.
Your speech should not only serve as a tribute to Jason's life but also as a source of comfort and healing for those mourning his loss. It should be delivered in a tone that is sincere, respectful, and reflective of the love and admiration felt for Jason.
answer:
We are gathered today to remember my brother, Jason Wilson, and to share the grief of losing someone who mattered to so many of us.

Jason was 67 when he died last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center. Those facts mark the end of his life, but they cannot contain all that his life meant. He was a brother, a friend, a colleague, and a member of this community. Each of us carries a different memory of him, and together those memories tell a fuller story.

Grief is the measure of how deeply someone has become part of our lives. It can be hard to imagine the days ahead without Jason in them. We do not have to hurry past that sadness. We can make room for it, and for gratitude too: gratitude that we knew him, that we shared time with him, and that his presence left its mark on us.

Today, let us remember Jason in the stories we tell and in the care we show one another. Let us support the people who are hurting, and carry forward what we valued in him. His life is over, but the love and memories he gave us remain part of our lives.

Jason, my brother, thank you for being part of ours. We will miss you, and we will remember you with love.
